text: The Beilinson-Bernstein theorem (1981) gives, for dominant $\lambda$, an equivalence between $\mathfrak{g}$-modules with generalized central character $\lambda$ and:
choices: Brauer characters of a finite group
explanation: Beilinson-Bernstein realizes such $\mathfrak{g}$-modules as $\mathcal{D}_\lambda$-modules on $G/B$, linking them to perverse sheaves via Riemann-Hilbert. Brauer characters and projective indecomposables are objects of modular representation theory of finite groups; automorphic forms live on the analytic side of the Langlands program.
